concept: Foundation of the Indian National Congress
question: Who among the following was one of the co - founders of the Swaraj Party within the Congress to argue for a return to council politics?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chittaranjan Das**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chittaranjan Das**, also known as **Deshbandhu**, was one of the prominent leaders of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He co-founded the **Swaraj Party** in 1923 along with **Motilal Nehru**.
 
• The purpose of the Swaraj Party was to enter the legislative councils through elections and obstruct the British government from within.
 
• Chittaranjan Das served as the **first president** of the Swaraj Party.
 
• The formation of the Swaraj Party marked a significant shift in the strategy of the Indian National Congress towards achieving self-governance.
 
• Das was a firm advocate of using legislative councils as a platform to voice the demands of Indians and to expose the inadequacies of British rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale**__

 __
 
• Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a senior leader of the Indian National Congress and a social reformer.
 
• He founded the **Servants of India Society** in 1905 to work for social reforms.
 
• He was a mentor to Mahatma Gandhi and emphasized constitutional methods for achieving self-rule.
 
 
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore**__
 __
 
• Rabindranath Tagore was a renowned poet, philosopher, and polymath.
 
• He was the first non-European to win the **Nobel Prize in Literature** in 1913.
 
• Tagore is best known for his literary works and his role in the cultural renaissance of India.
 
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**__
 
 
• Mahatma Gandhi was the foremost leader of the Indian independence movement.
 
• He is best known for his philosophy of **non-violent resistance** and civil disobedience.
 
• Gandhi led several major campaigns against British rule, including the Salt March and the Quit India Movement.
